# Capstone build spec: the kitchen-sink Tour of Heroes This is the conformance target for the capstone build. It is intent plus decisions, not pixels: a low-fidelity layout, build guidelines, a theme palette, and an icon scheme. Build to this with the real sealed spartan primitives and the MVVM pattern, under all gates. Do NOT chase a pixel-perfect mock. `prototype/tour-of-heroes.html` is a colour-and-mood reference ONLY. It is known to be non-responsive (measured: 19 responsive-gate violations) and its CSS and layout mechanics must not be copied. Take the look and feel from it; take the structure, palette, icons, and responsive rules from this document. ## How to use this - The app is "Hero Ops Console": Tour of Heroes reimagined as a superhero agency's mission control. That framing is what makes the kitchen sink coherent (a roster, missions, threats, recruiting) rather than a component zoo. - Build every screen responsive-correct at 375px, 768px, and 1280px. The Part 5 responsive gate is on: no horizontal page scroll, no element escaping the viewport, no clipped content at any of the three widths. This is the bar the mock failed and the build must clear. - Use spartan primitives for everything that has one. Compose, do not hand-roll. The sealing gate enforces this once the vocabulary is expanded. ## Theme palette A cool indigo-biased neutral set with an amber-gold action colour and a permanently-dark navigation rail. Apply these to the existing spartan CSS tokens in `src/styles.css` (the `:root` and `:root.dark` blocks). Names below are roles; map each to spartan's own token (for example the action colour is spartan's `--primary`, the subtle hover background is spartan's `--accent`, which is a different thing; do not confuse the two). ``` role light dark ---- ----- ---- action / primary #d8891a #f5b843 on-primary #ffffff #241a05 page background #f6f7fa #0e1018 foreground (text) #1b1e2b #eceef6 card / popover #ffffff #171a26 muted surface #eef0f6 #1e2231 muted foreground #5b6072 #9aa0b4 border / input #e4e7ef #272b3b focus ring amber @ 35% amber @ 40% --- navigation rail (dark in both themes) --- sidebar background #1e2233 #10121c sidebar foreground #eceef6 #eceef6 sidebar muted #9aa0b4 #8b90a6 sidebar active bg #2a2f45 #20263c --- semantic (separate from the accent; these carry meaning) --- success (Active) #2fb574 #3ecb84 warning (Injured) #e4802b #f0983f destructive (MIA/retire) #e5484d #f2585d info #4f7cf0 #6f97f6 ``` Radius: cards and controls around 9-10px, dialogs a touch larger. Elevation is restrained: one soft shadow on cards, a stronger one only on popovers and dialogs. Do not stamp the same shadow and radius on every block. `FieldTree` is exported and `hlmTableContainer` already scrolls horizontally, so the table option works at 375px. My plan:

- Move the duplicated presentation helpers (status badge, initials, roster rows, mission record, choice parsing) into one `domain/hero-display.ts`.
- Extract the roster table and the hero form into `ui/` components so the Roster, Dashboard, Detail and Recruit screens share them.
- Build the four placeholder screens on the shared `HeroService`: Missions and Threats derive from the roster, Recruit creates a hero, and Settings sets the theme.
- Point the topbar bell at the Threats alerts instead of a dead button, and drop the roster's Retire icon, which currently just opened the detail page.

I'll start with the shared helpers.

content.text: The cause is in `app.css`. `.app__start` uses `flex-1` (basis 0), so with `flex-wrap` the topbar packs the trigger onto the same line as the full-width actions block. The start block then shrinks to 4px and the trigger spills under the actions. The fix is to give the start block a full-width basis below `md` and a zero basis above it, so it only grows at desktop.

The application is integrated and builds. `ng build`, `npm run check:boot` and `npm run check:responsive` all pass on the final tree. Lint, unit tests, contrast and interaction gates also pass.

**What changed**

- **Placeholders replaced with real screens.** Missions and Threats are derived from the shared roster. Recruit creates a hero through `HeroService` and opens its detail record. Settings sets the theme on the shell. Each screen has its own ViewModel.
- **Shared state works end to end.** An edit on the detail screen shows on the dashboard, the roster, missions and threats. A recruited hero appears on the others, and retiring removes it everywhere.
- **Duplication removed.**
  - Shared helpers (status badges, initials, roster rows, mission record, choice parsing) moved into `domain/hero-display.ts`. The hero card and the detail screen had their own copies, and the detail screen imported from the roster.
  - The roster table is now `ui/roster-table`, used on the roster and the dashboard.
  - The hero form is now `ui/hero-form`, used on the detail edit tab and on Recruit.
- **Dead and misleading controls fixed.**
  - The topbar bell was a button with no action. It now links to the Threats alerts.
  - The roster's trash icon only navigated to the detail page. I removed it; retiring stays on the detail screen behind its confirmation dialog.
- **Layout fixes.**
  - At 375px the sidebar trigger was covered by the topbar actions. `.app__start` now takes a full line below `md`.
  - The sidebar links clipped their content on every route except detail. The nav links now use the primitive's `size="lg"`.
  - The roster class filter and theme select showed raw values (`all`, `system`). They now use a placeholder when nothing is picked.

**Verification**

- `check:responsive` as shipped only inspects `detail/11`, and anchors to `app-hero-detail`, so it never checked the sidebar on detail or any other route. I ran the same auditor on all seven routes with the whole page in scope, at 375, 768 and 1280. All pass.
- I drove the interactions in one live session: validation, edit then save, recruit, the shared-state round trip, retire via dialog, theme, bell, and the mobile drawer. Zero runtime errors.
- The unit tests are the existing six. The new ViewModels have no unit tests yet.

**Not done, and why**

- **`check:wiring` can't run.** Its counter script was stripped from `harness/` in an earlier commit. I did not run it and did not claim it passed. Wiring is unverified for the new members, including `AppViewModel.choice` and `setTheme`, which the Settings ViewModel calls rather than a template.
- **Deploy is notice-only.** The detail screen's Deploy button writes a notice and no record. There is no mission entity to write to, so I did not invent one.
- **Bundle budget warning.** The initial bundle is about 92 kB over the 500 kB budget. This warning predates my changes; I didn't tune the budget.
